principles.name: Selflessness
principles.def: Act solely in the public interest.

principles.name: Integrity
principles.def: Avoid obligations that could influence official duties.

principles.name: Objectivity
principles.def: Make choices on merit and evidence.

principles.name: Accountability
principles.def: Be accountable and submit to scrutiny.

principles.name: Openness
principles.def: Be as open as possible about decisions and actions.

principles.name: Leadership
principles.def: Promote and support these principles by example.

LGA.name: Local Government Association: Model Councillor Code of Conduct

selflessness.evidence: Holders of public office should act solely in terms of the public interest.

integrity.evidence: Should not place themselves under any financial or other obligation to outside individuals or organisations that might seek to influence them.

accountability.evidence: Accountable for their decisions and actions to the public and must submit themselves to whatever scrutiny is appropriate.

openness.evidence: Should be as open as possible about all the decisions and actions that they take.

honesty.evidence: A duty to declare any private interests relating to their public duties.

leadership.evidence: Should promote and support these principles by leadership and example (Seven Principles appendix).

coc.doc_type: LGA Model Councillor Code of Conduct
coc.note: Local councils adopt the LGA model code, which sets out the Seven Principles of Public Life; individual councils' codes are not separately assessed.

LGA.basis: Every council must adopt a code of conduct consistent with the seven principles (Localism Act 2011, ss. 27–28). Most model theirs on this LGA code.

CO.name: Cabinet Office: Code of Conduct for Board Members of Public Bodies (2019)

selflessness.evidence: Holders of public office should act solely in terms of the public interest.

integrity.evidence: Holders of public office must avoid placing themselves under any obligation to people or organisations that might try inappropriately to influence them in their work.

objectivity.evidence: Holders of public office must act and take decisions impartially, fairly and on merit, using the best evidence and without discrimination or bias.

accountability.evidence: Holders of public office are accountable to the public for their decisions and actions and must submit themselves to the scrutiny necessary to ensure this.

openness.evidence: Holders of public office should act and take decisions in an open and transparent manner.

honesty.evidence: Holders of public office should be truthful.

leadership.evidence: Holders of public office should exhibit these principles in their own behaviour. They should actively promote and robustly support the principles and be willing to challenge poor behaviour wherever it occurs.

coc.doc_type: Code of Conduct for Board Members of Public Bodies
coc.note: Applies to the non-executive board members of central government bodies; section 3 sets out the Seven Principles. Individual bodies are not separately assessed.

CO.basis: Applies to all non-executive members on the boards of government departments, non-ministerial departments, executive agencies, NDPBs and national public corporations, and forms part of their terms of appointment.
